questions.stem: Which instrument is traditionally called the 'Queen of Instruments' in Carnatic classical music?

options.option_text: Sitar — the primary plucked string instrument of North India
Veena — the ancient plucked string instrument of South India
Sarod — the fretless plucked string instrument of North India
Santoor — a hammered string instrument originating in Kashmir

questions.explanation: The Veena is revered as the 'Queen of Instruments' in Carnatic tradition and is iconographically associated with Goddess Saraswati. The Sitar is the emblematic melodic instrument of Hindustani music; the Sarod and Santoor are also North Indian instruments and carry no equivalent title in Carnatic music.

questions.stem: In a classical Hindustani or Carnatic recital, the 'alap' (alapana) performed at the outset primarily serves to?

options.option_text: Showcase the vocalist's speed in executing rapid taan passages
Introduce the tala cycle and establish the rhythmic foundation
Explore the raga's mood, grammar, and note relationships without rhythm
Demonstrate the artiste's ability to blend two ragas simultaneously

questions.explanation: Alap/alapana is performed without percussion; its sole purpose is to gradually unfold the raga — its characteristic notes, ornaments, and emotional color — at a free, improvised pace. Taans (rapid melodic runs) belong to the later bandish section, and tala is introduced only afterward. Raga blending is a separate concert device, not the function of alap.

questions.stem: Which of the following raga-to-time-of-day pairings is correctly matched according to the Hindustani 'prahar' (time-cycle) system?

options.option_text: Raga Yaman — prescribed for the pre-dawn morning hours
Raga Bhimpalasi — prescribed for the late-afternoon hours
Raga Darbari Kanada — prescribed for the midday hours
Raga Bhupali — prescribed for the deep midnight hours

questions.explanation: Bhimpalasi belongs to the 3rd prahar (roughly 3–6 PM) and is a standard late-afternoon raga. Yaman is an evening (4th prahar, sunset) raga, not a morning one — a common mix-up. Darbari Kanada is performed deep at night (7th–8th prahar), not at midday. Bhupali is also an evening raga, not associated with midnight.

questions.stem: The Khayal genre rose to dominance in Hindustani vocal music during the 18th century, largely through the patronage of which ruler who was himself an avid music lover?

options.option_text: Emperor Akbar, who hosted Tansen in his Navaratna court
Nawab Wajid Ali Shah of Avadh, patron of thumri and kathak
Muhammad Shah 'Rangila', the Mughal emperor who patronised Sadarang
Sultan Ibrahim Adil Shah II of Bijapur, the 'Jagat Guru' of arts

questions.explanation: Muhammad Shah 'Rangila' (r. 1719–48) patronised Nyamat Khan, who composed under the pen-name 'Sadarang', and his nephew Adarang; together they created thousands of khayal compositions and standardised the genre's form. Akbar's era is associated with Dhrupad and Tansen, not Khayal. Wajid Ali Shah championed thumri and kathak a century later.

questions.stem: In Carnatic classical music, the term 'Manodharma Sangita' collectively refers to which category of musical activity?

options.option_text: Kritis and varnas composed and fixed by the Carnatic Trinity
Improvised elements such as alapana, niraval, and kalpana swaras
The rhythmic framework formed by tala patterns and mridangam
The fixed ascending and descending scale pattern of a given raga

questions.explanation: Manodharma Sangita literally means 'music born of the imagination' and covers all improvised aspects: alapana (free raga elaboration), niraval (melodic variation over a lyric line), kalpana swaras (improvised solfège runs), and ragam-tanam-pallavi. Fixed compositions like kritis belong to 'Kalpita Sangita', not Manodharma — a distinction examiners frequently test.

questions.stem: The theoretical framework of 72 Melakarta ragas, which underpins the systematic classification of all Carnatic ragas, was first codified by which scholar?

options.option_text: Purandaradasa, who standardized the Carnatic teaching curriculum
Tyagaraja, who composed over a thousand kritis across many ragas
Venkatamakhi, author of the 17th-century treatise Chaturdandiprakasika
Muthuswami Dikshitar, who deliberately set kritis in all 72 melakartas

questions.explanation: Venkatamakhi (Venkatamakhin) systematised the 72-melakarta scheme in his Sanskrit treatise 'Chaturdandiprakasika' (17th century), constructing a mathematical grid of all possible heptatonic scales. Muthuswami Dikshitar is the most tempting distractor because he composed kritis in all 72 melakartas — but he used the existing scheme, he did not create it. Purandaradasa standardised pedagogical lesson sequences, not raga taxonomy.

questions.stem: The Bishnupur gharana of West Bengal holds a unique position in Hindustani music primarily because of which characteristic?

options.option_text: Being the sole surviving Hindustani Dhrupad tradition rooted in Bengal
Its pioneering synthesis of Hindustani ragas with Baul folk styles
Exclusively specializing in the rudra veena and been instruments
Having been founded personally by Tansen during Emperor Akbar's reign

questions.explanation: The Bishnupur gharana, patronised by the Malla kings of Bishnupur, is the only Hindustani Dhrupad tradition that took deep root in Bengal, with lineage traced to disciples of the Tansen-Senia tradition who migrated east. The Baul synthesis option is a plausible distractor but incorrect — Baul is a separate folk-devotional stream. Tansen himself never founded this gharana; his disciples did so after Akbar's era.
